WHAT WE RECORD An image request, not a person's attention For an eligible message, our application records when the measurement image is requested and a bounded count of requests. We report this as an image fetch. We do not record IP addresses or user-agent strings in this application measurement record. Our application measurement does not use cookies, device fingerprints or tracking parameters on the email's destination links. Normal hosting, gateway and security providers can still receive standard request and network metadata while serving an image, and may set security cookies for purposes such as bot protection. We do not use those infrastructure cookies in the application measurement record. The absence of IP addresses and user-agent strings from our application measurement table does not mean infrastructure never receives those fields. The Privacy Notice and Subprocessors and infrastructure page describe ordinary service handling. EVIDENCE LIMITS Image fetching does not confirm opening or delivery Email services, privacy proxies and security scanners may request or cache images automatically. A forwarded email can also cause a request associated with the original message. We cannot use an image request to identify who fetched it, establish that the intended recipient opened or read the email, count distinct readers, or prove inbox placement or successful delivery. An email with images blocked, cached or viewed as plain text may produce no request even when it is read. No recorded fetch means unknown, not unopened or undelivered. Sent-mail verification, provider acceptance and failure notices are separate evidence with their own limits; image-fetch records do not replace them. YOUR CONTROLS Opt-outs and replies stop future measurement You can select “Not interested” in the email and confirm, or reply “No thanks.” When you opt out or reply, we stop recording future image requests for the affected message and stop measurement for further outreach to that recipient. You can block remote images or use the plain-text alternative without losing the email's invitation, opt-out or public-resource links. COLLECTION AND CLEANUP A maximum 30-day collection window We stop collecting these image-request records no later than 30 days after the message is sent, or earlier when an opt-out or reply stops measurement. We do not extend the window because an image is fetched again. Expired measurement rows are excluded from current reporting and cleared through bounded cleanup when the image function is used or during a manual review. We do not promise that a timed background job deletes every row at the exact expiration instant. Ordinary invitation, suppression, delivery, legal and security records follow their separate purposes and retention rules in the Privacy Notice. SEPARATE FROM THE PRODUCT Website tracking stays retired This email-image supplement does not reactivate website measurement, reuse a retired website visit identifier, add labels to destination links, or treat an earlier browser choice or product acknowledgement as permission for new processing. People doing the work, managers and senior leaders can describe the same work differently. A responsibility that seems clear to one person may be uncertain to another. A decision that appears straightforward may pass through several reviews before anything happens.

Q²-SODI gives those perspectives a common starting point. Each person answers a structured set of questions. The software brings the findings into clear reports, helping you ask better questions, identify priorities and make informed choices about improvement.

Qualitative perspectives. Quantitative results. The two Qs stand for qualitative and quantitative: how your people describe the work, together with structured numerical results that help you see patterns and compare over time. SODI names the four diagnostics: Structural Clarity, Operational Systems, Decision Velocity and Institutional Performance.

Start with a team, department, process or decision path. Extend the view across your organization as the work develops.

How to read Diagnostic and Synthesis results

Q²-SODI has four diagnostics: Structural Clarity, Operational Systems, Decision Velocity, and Institutional Performance. One run produces an individual report. The four diagnostic examples here go a step further: each compares responses from 15 people in an organization with 30 eligible participants. They show differences in experience and practical next steps while more responses are collected. These examples are not yet eligible for Depth Synthesis and do not present organizational savings.

Depth Synthesis examines responses to one diagnostic once the campaign meets its evidence requirements. Cross-Lens Synthesis brings eligible results from multiple diagnostics together, keeping differences visible. One person is counted once within each lens and once across the campaign, even if they complete all four diagnostics. The Workspace shows what is ready and what is still needed. The Synthesis examples include separate operating records and change assumptions to estimate time, spending and capacity benefits. Staff capacity is time available for other work, not automatically cash savings.

Structural Clarity tests the domain statement directly: can the people executing a principle state what it is for and where it stops? Overrun begins exactly where boundary-knowledge ends, and the earliest measurable signal is the gap between leadership’s stated purpose for a principle and the operating rule the floor has actually inferred. Operational Systems audits processes as frozen principles, sorting the ones still serving their founding purpose from the ones now running on fidelity alone. Decision Velocity locates the stopping rules in decision rights: whether reviews are pre-committed or improvised, and how the speed of reversing a decision compares with the speed of making one – an organization that cannot reverse faster than it commits has brakes in name only. And Institutional Performance is where inversion surfaces as fact: the founding principle’s own outcome measures moving against the principle’s intent.

Structural Clarity tests the domain statement directly: can the people executing a principle state what it is for and where it stops? Overrun begins exactly where boundary-knowledge ends, and the earliest measurable signal is the gap between leadership’s stated purpose for a principle and the operating rule the floor has actually inferred. Decision Velocity locates the stopping rules in decision rights: whether reviews are pre-committed or improvised, and how the speed of reversing a decision compares with the speed of making one – an organization that cannot reverse faster than it commits has brakes in name only. Operational Systems audits processes as frozen principles, sorting the ones still serving their founding purpose from the ones now running on fidelity alone. And Institutional Performance is where inversion surfaces as fact: the founding principle’s own outcome measures moving against the principle’s intent.

How Monderman applies the distinction

Examine a defined operating scope alongside reported experience.

Monderman’s four Diagnostics collect structured responses about related parts of organizational work. Structural Clarity addresses ownership, authority, and handoffs. Operational Systems addresses process burden. Decision Velocity addresses approvals, escalation, and routing. Institutional Performance addresses the broader operating system.

Each result describes the completed responses within a defined run scope. It is not an external observation or an organization-wide finding.

Depth Synthesis summarizes eligible runs from one Diagnostic. Cross-Lens Synthesis compares eligible results from different Diagnostics and publishes a Composite Score only when the selected evidence meets the platform’s coherence rules.

The studies cited here did not test or validate Monderman’s instruments. They support examining management practices and organizational mechanisms as a distinct layer of organizational evidence.
